scopeReview: IMP-2.E.1: economic, political and cultural effects at origins/destinations. Remittances, skilled-workforce balance, knowledge transfer, labor matching, care, culture, fiscal/electoral limits and composition. Conditional, heterogeneous effects; no real-world financial/legal advice or universal fiscal/wage claim.
varietyReview: Fee table, mixed-unit reverse flows, workforce ledger and cultural-establishment bars. Other applied mechanisms include return skills, labor complementarity, political eligibility, household responsibilities, adaptation and time horizons. All five skills, varied keys/difficulty.
repetitionReview: Unlike2.10 causes and2.11 types, items assess consequences. Reverse flows use different units, not another net-people subtraction. Workforce entries/exits and net-zero age change differ from total-population accounting; cultural continuity/adaptation is grounded in an original scenario.
referenceNote: Primary development research corroborates possible remittance/knowledge benefits and skilled-worker costs. All scenario numbers/figures/questions original; no survey/GDP estimates copied or third-party resources added. No independent human review claimed.

questions.correctOption: The recipient receives 30 additional units, with no increase in the gross amount sent.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed1000−50=950 and1000−20=980, difference30. Gross amount, earnings and net receipt are distinct; no exchange-rate or extra-charge assumption introduced.

questions.correctOption: People move toward B while remittance money flows toward A; these quantities cannot be combined as one people balance.
questions.independentReview: Read A→B800people and B→A200000currency separately. Verified opposite arrow endpoints and unit labels; no numerical population balance can mix these units or establish return movement.

questions.correctOption: 185; skilled emigration can reduce service capacity when not fully offset by other entries.
questions.independentReview: Independently balanced start200+trained30−retired10−emigrated40+immigrated5=185. Natural workforce entries/exits differ from migration; no universal claim that skilled migration always harms origins or that headcount alone measures care quality.

questions.correctOption: The destination’s commercial landscape incorporates cultural practices carried by migrants.
questions.independentReview: Verified restaurants4→12 and specialty shops2→8 with migrant ownership/origin practices explicitly supplied. Inference concerns visible commercial culture, not all residents’ behavior or a population count.

questions.correctOption: Return and transnational connections can transfer knowledge as well as money.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished a specific return-mediated knowledge transfer from a guarantee about every emigrant. The example complements, rather than erases, the separate possibility of origin skilled-worker shortages.

questions.correctOption: Successful matching can fill some vacancies and expand productive activity.
questions.independentReview: Checked compatibility between skill supply and specified vacancies, with access/recognition constraints retained. No inevitable aggregate wage, employment or shortage result is asserted.

questions.correctOption: Voting eligibility, participation and political preferences among the affected residents.
questions.independentReview: Separated population arrival from eligibility, turnout and preference. Avoided any current-country voting-law claim or assumption that migrants form a homogeneous voting bloc.

questions.correctOption: Changes in local labor availability and the distribution of care responsibilities.
questions.independentReview: Traced a selective adult outflow to potential village labor/care changes while retaining household variation and unmeasured transfers. Did not assume that all remaining older people are dependent or every household is harmed.

questions.correctOption: Cultural continuity and adaptation can occur together in the same community.
questions.independentReview: Compared retained festival and adopted institutional language as different cultural dimensions. Coexistence follows directly, while complete isolation or total replacement would contradict one of the stated facts.

questions.correctOption: Compare costs and contributions over time, including differences among groups and government levels.
questions.independentReview: Separated short-run local expenditures from later and possibly differently allocated revenues. No real budget estimate or universal fiscal sign is inferred; heterogeneous outcomes remain an empirical question.

questions.correctOption: The age composition changes because arrivals and departures involve different cohorts.
questions.independentReview: Independently checked total0, older−100 and ages20–29+100 under no other changes. No birth, death, employment or exact service-demand outcome is invented.
